_comment: The judges the seeded meets are staffed from, and the ONE place they are named.
Committed and hand-maintained, read by both stacks: Web/e2e/support/judge-roster.js
registers them through the UI, and Server/scripts/planPanels.js draws panel seats
from them. The seat emails used to be hardcoded in planPanels.js as a six-entry
object, separately from the roster that created those accounts -- so seating a
judge who had never registered failed deep inside the admin screen with a name
that was simply not in the search results.
Email and password are DERIVED, never stored here:
email     firstname.<first letter of surname>@gmail.com, lowercase
password  <Firstname>@2026
Both sides derive them the same way -- see people.js on the Web side and the
emailFor helper in lib/judges.js on the Server side.
Sixteen of them, so the twelve meets can be staffed by different panels rather
than the same six people everywhere. A panel needs six seats (Senior Judge,
Judge 1-4, Scorer), and the schema forbids one person holding two seats on the
SAME panel -- but the same person sitting at several MEETS is normal, and is
exactly what the post-login level flow exists to let them switch between.
certificationLevel is a judging CREDENTIAL and has nothing to do with the
competition level -- it collides by name and uses different casing. It does not
gate which meets a judge may be seated at; see Web/README.md.
Mayur Pashte and Preetesh Gamre also appear on the player and coach rosters.
Each role is a separate collection with its own unique index on email, so that
is three independent accounts, not a collision.
